newsitem.title: INDIA: Three die in India tower block blaze.
newsitem.headline: Three die in India tower block blaze.

text.p: Three people died and nearly 30 people were rescued from a fire on the upper floors of a 25-storey building in India's financial capital Bombay on Wednesday, officials said.
"Three people died in a room on the twenty-second floor that had been locked on the inside," city official Shridhar Joshi told Reuters.
Joshi said the three men were employees of Pfizer Ltd, a pharmaceutical company. One body had been identified, he added.
"Since the room was locked the firemen thought there was nobody inside, and so there was some delay," he said.
A fire control room official said firefighters had put out the flames on the twenty-first floor, where the blaze apparently started, and had nearly extinguished the fire on the higher levels.

The Express Towers, in the prestigious Nariman Point business district, houses the Indian Express newspaper on the ground and first floor, and a number of domestic and multinational companies and banks have offices on the higher levels.
